changes: Title, multi-line join by column (pick_title + new column_neighbor): the next line above or below is no longer the next reading-order index. It is the closest line by edge gap among lines that overlap horizontally, so slogan, date or venue lines in a side column that fall between two title lines in reading order are skipped. All the old join conditions are unchanged: height at least 0.62 of the best line, gap at most 0.9 of its height, no two complete suffix lines, no digit-only lines, no Latin-only line under a Hangul title, at most 3 lines. Fixes paddle v2-066 '안동국제 / 탈춤페스티벌' and v2-086 '용인사이버 / 과학축제', and lowers title CER on all 3 pipelines.

Title, glued English variant removed (new drop_latin_tail in title_text): inside one OCR record, a Latin run of 4 or more letters stuck to the end of a Hangul title with no space ('진연Jinyeon' -> '진연') is cut off. This extends the existing rule that already drops Latin-only records from Hangul titles. Latin separated by a space ('동구 HARMONY FESTIVAL') is kept because it can be part of the name. Characters are only cut, never changed. Fixes v2-001 on easyocr 2x and 1x.

Title, a lone suffix word gets no bonus: the +3 suffix bonus now needs at least 1 name letter before the suffix, so a line that is only 'Festival' or '축제' does not score as a title. One-syllable names like '북 페스티벌' still qualify. Only paddle v2-099 changes on dev ('Festival' -> '가을'): CER improves a little, exact match does not change.

Year, year glued to the month: YEAR also matches 20[2-3]X when it is immediately followed by a month (01-12), a dot or slash, and a digit ('202609. 18'), i.e. the OCR dropped the separator. This only finds a boundary; no character is changed. Fixes year (and schedule start_year) for v2-047 easyocr 1x.

Edition, Korean word ordinals as a fallback (new EDITION_WORD / ORDINAL_KO): '첫/두/세/…/열 번째' maps to 1-10. It is used only when no numeric edition matches and only on short lines (10 Hangul characters or fewer). Fixes v2-144 '첫 번째 이야기' on easyocr 2x and 1x.

Not in change.diff: the candidate file has one extra line, marked '# PROPOSAL-SHIM', that finds ROOT by walking up to the folder containing data/festivals/poster.template.json. Without it the copy cannot run from .runtime/ under rule_dev. I left it out of change.diff so it will not conflict with other proposals; the diff applies cleanly to app/poster_ocr/extract.py (checked with patch --dry-run).

Tried and dropped: (a) a penalty for sentence endings in -다/-요: no effect on dev. (b) a size cap on joined lines (at most 1.6x the best line): broke the two-tier title v2-135 '경산대추축제 / & 농산물 한마당' and raised easyocr CER. (c) a higher OCR-confidence weight (1.8 or 2.4): +1 exact on easyocr 2x (v2-097) but higher CER on both easyocr pipelines. (d) accepting a bare 'N회' with any leading glyph: it would fix 3 edition cases ('게16회' x2, '저26회'), but only by treating misread 게/저 as 제, which the no-correction rule forbids. (e) a tie-break that prefers the upper line (v2-029): fits an arbitrary labeling choice.

proposals.field_group: schedule: start/end dates, printed weekday, year basis, cross-line date ranges, operating times (schedule.times), duration_raw
changes: Commas are now accepted where a period is expected in a date: year, month and day separators ('2026,9.18.', '09,.11') and the mark after the day ('10.2,(금)'). A doubled range separator such as '10.17.--10.25' counts as one. Up to two opening brackets may come before the weekday ('10.2.[(금]~10.4.[일]').

Weekdays: English 2-letter abbreviations (MO TU WE TH FR SA SU) and full English names (FRIDAY) are now read. A '일' glued right after a dotted M.D ('09.13일)', '10.18일', '10.18 일') is read as Sunday only when the calendar says that date is a Sunday; otherwise it stays a day suffix. Weekday checks now happen while candidates are built, using the poster year (default 2026).
Month and day separated only by a space ('10 25 (일)', '10 1목)', '2026. 10 25. (일)') are accepted only when a printed weekday follows and that weekday matches the calendar.

Range with no separator: the end may be day-only if its printed weekday matches the calendar ('2026.9.18(금) 20(일)'). The end may have a month but no readable weekday if the start weekday matches the calendar and the end is terminated ('10.17.토 10.18.'). The slash form 'M/D M/D' is also accepted. A regex lookahead stops this pattern from matching a bare trailing number such as '10.3(토) 3층', which protects the venue text-stripping.

Unreadable weekday slot: one noise character between the start date and the range separator is skipped, but only when the end date has an explicit month ('10.23.0~10.25.@', '10.24.9~10.25.@'). Such candidates get a -1 score penalty.

Cross-line dates: a line holding only a date (one leftover letter or digit allowed: '9.12', '10. 18.', '10.9. @') becomes a weak single candidate. It can win only when nothing better exists, or it can pair with a nearby line of similar height. A single that joins a year on the line above ('2026.' + '10.7.수') can now also be a pair partner, with distance measured from its month/day line.

Multi-period schedules: if the chosen one-line range is directly followed by an aligned, same-size line that starts with a later range and otherwise holds only weekday or '매주/주말/매일' text, the end date moves to that range's end (120-day cap). A line like '10.10 ~ 10.11 사전행사' does not extend it.

Times: '.' or ',' is accepted as the hour-minute separator only before minutes '00', since 'M.00' can never be a date ('12.00-17.00', '10:00-21.00', '16,00-20,00'). When the start clock is explicit, the end clock may be HHMM with no separator ('12.00-1700'). The start time is never inferred from HHMM.

proposals.field_group: venue raw/items (label-based and keyword-based selection, multi-line venues, venue on the same line as dates), address, admin_area
changes: The venue logic now lives in a new pick_venue() function. Selection order is unchanged: label, then the schedule line, then keyword lines. Only the rules inside each step changed.

Label: a mid-line label is accepted when it has a colon ('일정: … / 장 소: …', VENUE_LABEL_MID). For a label-only line ('장소' read as its own box), the value is taken from the same row to its right (same_row_value) before falling back to the next line.

Venue on the same line as dates: venue_segment() splits the schedule line at the date/time matches and keeps the piece that has a venue word ('동영 트라이애습총광장 11.6(금)-8 …' -> the venue part). Date labels like '일시' are removed only at word boundaries, so '제일시장' stays intact.

clean_venue(): drops leading date leftovers (pieces with at most 1 Hangul letter, no Latin letters and some digit or symbol, e.g. '10 1목)-', '(금]~ |', '0'), leading bullets, a trailing '※ …' notice and trailing #hashtags. It never changes characters, and keeps Latin-led text such as 'K-55'.

strip_dates() / mark_dates(): dates are removed only when month is 1-12 and day 1-31, and not when the number follows a digit or 로/길/번지/동/리. This stops the old removal from cutting '26-17' out of '한풍루로 326-17'.

Keyword fallback: lines with a run of 5 or more digits (phone or account fragments) are excluded. When no schedule was parsed, the line with the most M.D date fragments is used as the anchor instead of picking the top-most line.

Multi-line venues: the gap between lines may now be slightly negative (-0.35h, boxes touching or overlapping). The next line must overlap horizontally, and a '장소' label sitting between value lines is skipped. A line ending in , 및 · / | & pulls in the next line (up to 3 lines). The line above is joined when it is aligned and the same size and contains a venue word (not a title, role, phone or date line). Venues found through a label never join the line above.
VENUE_WORD gains 시청|군청|구청|도청 and '역' at the end of a line (not after 지/구/영/전, which excludes 지역/구역/영역/전역).
A venue printed as 'venue name | address' or 'venue name / address' is cut before the address, which stays in the address slot.

Address (address_in): the raw value is now the address itself, starting at the first 시·도/시·군·구/읍·면 within 25 characters before the road or lot match (plus an optional ', N층'), instead of the whole line. A lot-number address needs an area word before it. A road address without one needs a hyphenated or multi-digit number. This rejects noise like '미스트로4', '기리7', '치가6'.

Admin area: districts are searched after removing the 시·도 name and an optional '시' ('강원특별자치도철원군' -> 철원군, '울산중구' -> 중구, '충남계룡시일원' -> 계룡시). Words ending in 지구/입구/출구/항구, and 4+ letter words ending in 포구 ('소래포구'), are not districts. All different districts on the first line that has one are joined ('진도군, 해남군'; adjacent ones like '전주시 완산구' are joined with a space). If the venue and address lines give no 시·도 or no district, the title lines are used. This block now runs after title selection; title selection does not depend on it.

changes: Organizations, row reading: new organization_items() works on OCR records instead of build_lines lines. build_lines only appends records to the right, so a role label met after the names to its right (e.g. paddle '주최'|'국가유산청'|...|'주관'|'경주문화원') ended up alone on its own line. For each label record it gathers the records at the same height (vertical overlap >= 50%, height ratio 0.55-1.8) and reads them left to right from the leftmost label in the row. Records stacked vertically and overlapping horizontally become one two-line name. A gap over 2.5x the label height clears the current label until the next label appears. Names from a separate record need at least 2 Hangul syllables (drops logo junk like 'TON').

Organizations, ROLE_MARK: a role word preceded by a Hangul syllable is not taken as a label ('이이주관광당', '국제협력단'). '공동주최/공동주관' is accepted, and '및', '-', '&', 'ㆍ' (U+119E after NFKC) are accepted between 주최 and 주관 to mean host+organizer. role_raw keeps the printed label. The original ROLE regex is left unchanged because venue code still uses it.

Organizations, name cleanup: a phone number and empty parentheses stuck to a name are removed instead of the whole name being dropped ('주관: 산북품실축제위원회 (031.883.0031)' -> organizer 산북품실축제위원회). A trailing '문의/TEL' is stripped, and U+1175 (NFKC of 'ㅣ') counts as a separator.

Organizations, unlabeled_institutions(): a record in the top 12% or bottom 15% of the poster whose whole text is an admin-area name (ADMIN_NAME: province names, or 1-4 syllables + 시/군/구 optionally followed by another 시/군/구) or a Hangul name ending in an institution suffix (재단/공사/공단/문화원/위원회/협의회/진흥원/센터/은행/본부/협회/조합/일보/청/부) is added with roles=[] and role_raw=None, so no role is inferred. Excluded: lines already used by other fields, role/notice text, endings in NOT_DISTRICT, 신청/요청/일부/전부/내부/외부. This affects org presence only; roles=[] items are not counted in org F1.

Contacts: new PHONE_RUN reads a number whose second separator the OCR dropped ('02-21274231' -> value 02-2127-4231; the digits themselves are not changed). clock_span() rejects 4-4 'service numbers' where both halves are on-the-hour or half-past times in increasing order ('1900-2200' is 19:00-22:00).

Links: sns_handle() keeps an '@handle' only if it has >= 5 characters, >= 3 letters and more letters than digits (drops '@ONA', '@son', '@slon', '@23747.d'). LINK_SPACED is a fallback, used only when LINK finds nothing on the line, for 'www' addresses whose dots were read as spaces ('WWW YUDEUNG com'); raw is kept exactly as OCR read it.

Notices: is_notice() replaces NOTICE.search for the notices list only; the title-exclusion rule still uses NOTICE unchanged. It drops lines that are only '※' plus fewer than 3 letters, ignores 'OO 주차장' place names (but keeps 주차장 협소/부족/혼잡/만차/없/이용불가), and adds the transport/operation words 하차, 셔틀, 휴관, 교통통제, 조기 소진/마감/종료.
Badges: BADGE_MORE adds selection and support-programme statements ('축제/사업 선정', '선정 축제/사업', '지원사업', '공모사업'). badge_kind returns 'other' for 지원사업/공모사업.

Budget: BUDGET also accepts the label '사업비' (the dev gold v2-185 prints '사업비:190,000천원'; not measurable on dev because OCR never read that line). krw(): for a plain-won amount (no 억/천만/백만/만 unit) written in 3-digit groups, '.' is treated as a grouping mark because won amounts have no decimals ('65,500.000원' -> 65,500,000). issues.problem: extend_multi_period builds the chosen range's end date as date(end['year'] or year, ...) with no year rollover. For a cross-year range with no year on the start date, e_val ends up before s_val. Any range on the next line then passes the 'o_start > e_val' test. Repro: poster(('2026 겨울빛축제',80), ('12.28 ~ 1.3',30), ('12.30 ~ 12.31',30)) gives end 2026-12-31. The baseline gives 2027-01-03. The result is a wrong core date with no error raised.
issues.fix: Apply the same rollover that pick_schedule uses: `e_year = end["year"] or (year + 1 if (end["month"], end["day"]) < (start["month"], start["day"]) else year)`, then `if not _valid(e_year, end["month"], end["day"]): return best` and `e_val = date(e_year, end["month"], end["day"])`. Verified: the repro now gives 2027-01-03, multi_ok still extends 10.03 to 10.11, and dev numbers are unchanged.

issues.problem: `row[next(i for i, r in enumerate(row) if ROLE_MARK.search(...))]` has no default value. A role-mark record with zero or negative height fails its own row test (the height ratio is 0, or the overlap is negative). It is then not in `row`, so next() raises StopIteration. That aborts the whole rule_dev or run_dir batch, not just one document. Repro: [rec('주최',[10,850,100,820]), rec('강릉시',[110,820,200,850])] crashes, while the baseline returns a valid doc. A single zero-height '주최 강릉시' record also crashes. No dev OCR record has this shape (min height 3.5), so the bug is latent.
issues.fix: `first = next((i for i, r in enumerate(row) if ROLE_MARK.search(texts[r["id"]])), None)`, then `if first is None: continue`, then `for r in row[first:]:`.

issues.problem: There are divisions by line height with no guard: `prev['h'] / first['h']`, `nxt['h'] / last['h']` and `nxt['h'] / line['h']`. A zero-height venue line raises ZeroDivisionError at line 763, a new crash path; the baseline produced a document in this case. Zero-area boxes also make evidence bboxes schema-invalid in both versions. All-zero boxes already crash the baseline.
issues.fix: At the top of extract(), before build_lines, drop degenerate records: `records = [r for r in records if r["bbox_xyxy"][2] > r["bbox_xyxy"][0] and r["bbox_xyxy"][3] > r["bbox_xyxy"][1]]`. This only checks the input; it does not correct any characters. Verified: all synthetic zero-height and inverted cases now give valid docs, with no dev change.

issues.problem: Backtracking grows polynomially when a long run of whitespace follows a date or time. The cause is 4 or more adjacent optional \s* (after sd, in _wd, in RANGE_GAP and in RANGE_SEP), and the merged code also runs RANGE_NOSEP_RE over every line in strip_dates. A '10.18' followed by N spaces and 'x' takes 2.9 s at N=200 (baseline 0.9 s) and 245 s at N=800 (baseline 72 s). The time regex is the same in both (about 7.8 s at N=800). This is latent: the longest whitespace run in real dev OCR is 3.
issues.fix: Collapse whitespace in the matching text only: `line["norm"] = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", norm(line["text"]))` in build_lines. Raw fields still come from line['text'], and org_names' `\s{2,}` split runs on record text, not line norm. Verified: date+spaces at N=800 drops to 7.6 ms and time+spaces to 0.9 ms, with no dev change.

issues.problem: Two-letter English weekday codes are case-insensitive and need only `(?![a-z])` after them. So the ordinal in '2026.10.4th' is read as weekday 'thu' (10-04 is a Sunday), and '2026.10.1 We love it' is read as 'wed'. The baseline gives None for both. In dev OCR this pattern hits one ordinal ('The 12th', paddle v2-007) and one noise string ('u8Sa'). Its only genuine hit is '2026.9.18.FR -20'.
issues.fix: Accept two-letter codes in uppercase only: `WD_EN = r"(?:(?i:(?:mon|tue|wed|thu|fri|sat|sun)[a-z]{0,6}(?![a-z]))|(?:MO|TU|WE|TH|FR|SA|SU)(?![A-Za-z]))"`. Verified: 'FR' is still read, '4th' and 'We' give None, and dev is unchanged.

issues.problem: The hard-coded 2026 fallback year was previously used only for scoring. It now decides whether a candidate is accepted at all: spaced 'M D (요일)', '일' read as Sunday, and the end-weekday check for nosep ranges. A poster with no year printed on a 2027 calendar ('10 24 (일)') is rejected, while '10 25 (일)' is accepted. This is an assumption about the dataset year, not a general poster rule.
issues.fix: Make it a named, documented constant (e.g. DEFAULT_YEAR = 2026, with a comment that it is the collection year). Or, when poster_year is None, skip the readings that depend on the calendar check (ssp, esp, the 일-as-Sunday rule). If you choose the second option, measure it on dev before adopting it.

issues.problem: A line holding only 'M.D' (e.g. '3.5') is now a standalone schedule candidate. A poster with only a title and a '3.5' line gets schedule 03-05, where the baseline returned absent. The merged candidate is worth accepting once five small fixes are applied. I found one real date bug and some crash and slow-regex paths that the 60 dev cases never trigger.

**Checks**
- **Unit tests:** test_merged.py passes 8/8, and tests/test_poster_ocr.py (which still tests the baseline) passes 8/8.
- **Schema:** rule_dev reports 0 schema-invalid documents for every combo.
- **Dev results:** no case lost any field on any engine compared with the baseline, and every summary field stayed level or improved. The one weak spot is organization precision on paddleocr, which fell (FP 14 to 26) even though F1 rose.
- **Principles:** the extractor has no case ids, gold, file-name or TourAPI access, and no festival-specific literals in code. The new word lists are generic Korean poster vocabulary. Comments quote dev OCR strings, but no logic depends on them.

**Date logic**
- Cross-year handling is correct in pick_schedule and extract.
- A single date and a same-day range both give end = null.
- An end before the start rejects the range and falls back to the start date, same as the baseline. An invalid date such as Feb 29 2026 gives absent.
- One bug: extend_multi_period skips the year rollover, so a cross-year range followed by a range inside it gets its end shortened (2027-01-03 becomes 2026-12-31).

**Robustness**
- Empty input, one record, blank text and vertical boxes all work.
- A zero-height or inverted role-mark box makes organization_items raise StopIteration. Because rule_dev and run_dir don't catch errors from extract, this aborts the whole batch.
- A zero-height venue line raises ZeroDivisionError.
- A date followed by a long run of whitespace backtracks polynomially: 245 s at 800 spaces, against 72 s for the baseline.
- Real dev OCR has none of these shapes (min box height 3.5, longest whitespace run 3, longest text 77 characters), so all of them are latent.
- Case-insensitive two-letter English weekday codes misread '4th' as Thursday and 'We' as Wednesday.

**Fixes verified on a scratch copy** (F1 to F5): a default value for next(), dropping zero-area or inverted records at the top of extract(), the year rollover in extend_multi_period, collapsing whitespace in line['norm'], and uppercase-only two-letter weekdays. With them, every crash case gives a valid document, the cross-year end stays 2027-01-03, the slow cases take 1 to 8 ms, and the 8 unit tests pass. Dev metrics are identical to the unmodified merge on every engine.

**Tested but not recommended:** dropping lone weak 'M.D' singles (F6). It loses one schedule pair on each easyocr variant and one venue case on easyocr/rgb_2x.

**Lower-severity items:** the 2026 fallback year now decides whether some candidates are accepted at all, and the PROPOSAL-SHIM ROOT line must be reverted before promoting. The logged numbers are also stale: paddleocr n keeps growing (41 to 53) during the review, and hybrid/rgb_2x has no outputs, so it is unevaluated.
